name: The Peck household
head: peck_philip

arrival.note: Month precision. data/structures/peck_store.json records the arrival in July 1831 with a stock of goods in a schooner, from Andreas.

reason_for_coming.value: To open a store with a shipped stock of goods
reason_for_coming.note: He came with the goods, which is the merchant's version of coming with a contract.

lives_at.note: A merchant of this period lived over or behind his store, and this one demonstrably housed a lodger in its loft. Not stated of Peck himself.

persons.name: Philip F. W. Peck

occupation.note: 'P. F. W. Peck, merchant' in the 1833 roster. His two-storey frame store at the south-west corner of South Water and LaSalle is the anchor of the town's business street in this dataset.

persons.note: HIS UNFINISHED LOFT IS THE PARCEL'S BEST DOCUMENTED LODGING. Andreas: 'Among these was P. F. W. Peck, who invited Mr. Porter to make his temporary lodging place and study in the unfinished loft of his two-story store'; and 'The first building in the rear of this store was the log house of Rufus Brown, where Mr. Porter found table board.' Three households and two buildings meet in those two sentences. He arrived in July 1831 with a stock of goods carried by schooner, per this project's building record. Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named'. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Peck, P. F. W.” (tax_1833_083, line 135); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Peck, P. F. W.” (poll_1834_088, line 257). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Peck' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

research_note: THE HOUSEHOLD AT THE CENTRE OF A THREE-WAY LINK. Peck's store lodged the Presbyterian minister in its loft and Rufus Brown's log boarding house stood directly behind it - so a single corner of South Water and LaSalle carries a merchant, a minister and a boarding-house keeper, all documented, all in this parcel. That is the density the inferred phase should expect to find everywhere and can only demonstrate here.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
